clauses.reason: The clause directs the Administrator of General Services to designate the Mississippi National Space Technology Laboratories facilities as the John C. Stennis Space Center, to be known and referred to by that name thereafter. The naming rule continues; 51 U.S.C. 20306 (held current Code) refers to the center described in Executive Order 12641 as of the 2025 appropriation, and no held source ends the designation or shows it was reversed.

research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 12641 of May 20, 1988, 53 FR 18816 (May 24, 1988), held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12641.txt; the held text begins with a page header that the inventory span includes. It directs the Administrator of General Services to designate the facilities of the National Space Technology Laboratories of NASA in Mississippi as the John C. Stennis Space Center, which shall thereafter be known and referred to by that name. Current-law leads: the only mention is 51 U.S.C. 20306, a statutory text reference in the held current Code that treats the center as described in the order; no U.S. Code note, CFR citation, OFR disposition note or later order text cites the order (searches of held texts find only the order itself). Whether the General Services Administrator carried out the designation is not shown by a held source; the clause also states a continuing naming rule (such facilities shall thereafter be known by that name) that the 2025 statute applies, so the clause is claimed operative rather than ended by performance. Bounded searches read for coverage: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121 USLM text and notes, citations of the order by number, edition current through 2026-10-09, laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 plus GovInfo CFR bulk XML, 49 titles) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes of 6941 catalog records plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts).
